dedupe_keys.name: riddrp risk informed decision dependent resilience planning of transmission systems against ice storms

description: RIDDRP is a two-stage risk-informed decision-dependent resilience planning model for transmission systems facing ice storms, proposed in an October 2023 arXiv paper. The authors argue that traditional approaches overlook the endogenous uncertainty introduced by human decisions and underuse predictive information such as forecast accuracy and preparation time. The first stage makes line hardening decisions and the siting and sizing of energy storage; the second stage evaluates risk-informed operation costs, covering pre-event preparation and emergency operations, with line failure uncertainty that depends on the planning decisions as well as on exogenous ice storm uncertainty. A dual-objective approach balances economic efficiency and resilience in normal and emergent conditions. Case studies show that the model leverages predictive information for more judicious investment and better use of dispatchable resources, and the paper quantifies the impact of different properties of the predictive information. Access: the paper on arXiv, free; no code or licence is stated on the pages read. Caveats: an optimisation formulation on test cases. It suits transmission resilience investment studies, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
